# Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta (SN 35)
**ID:** SN 35
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn35
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0304m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Notable suttas feature senior disciples and key doctrinal similes. These include Upasena's death by snakebite (SN 35.69), Mahākaccāna's expositions to the householder Hāliddikāni (SN 35.130) and the pupils of the brahmin Lohicca (SN 35.132) [Nyanaponika et al. 2003], sense restraint as a generator of joy and concentration (SN 35.97) [Anālayo 2019], the definition of the "world" through the internal sense spheres (SN 35.116) [Wen], contemplation of rising and falling at the sense doors (SN 35.153) [Wen], and the famous simile of the fortified city and the pair of messengers (SN 35.204) [Marino 2017; Anālayo 2014].
Curated parallels in SuttaCentral connect SN 35 heavily to the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99, with 79 full parallels), as well as to the Chinese *Madhyamāgama* (MĀ 114 to SN 35.103), *Divyāvadāna* (ch. 2 to the *Puṇṇasutta*, SN 35.88), Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośopāyikā-ṭīkā*, and Sanskrit Turfan fragments (SHT Sutta 71) [SuttaCentral]. In Gāndhārī, manuscripts from the Senior collection preserve texts parallel to its *Samuddavagga* and *Āsīvisavagga* sections, such as the *Dārukkhandhopama* and city-simile discourses [Marino 2017]. Machine text-reuse matches in DharmaNexus similarly show extensive Pali sharing—predominantly with the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), and the *Aṅguttaranikāya*—and confirm close alignments with Chinese Āgamas (T 99, T 100), Tibetan Upāyikā texts (D 4094), and Sanskrit works like the *Saṅghabhedavastu* and *Avadānaśataka* [DharmaNexus].
